## Natural history notes

A small tree frog characterized by smooth skin, rounded toe pads, and highly variable coloration, ranging from green to brown, gray, or mottled patterns, often with a pale stripe along the side. In Florida, the Squirrel Tree Frog is widespread in pine flatwoods, hammocks, wetlands, gardens, parks, yards, ditches, and around buildings, especially after warm rains. It feeds on small insects and other invertebrates, calling from low vegetation, shrubs, or even walls and windows near lights, and breeding in temporary pools, roadside ditches, and shallow wetlands.
